episodes.title: She Grew Up in a Family Cult: Religious Trauma & Coercive Control | Stella McCormick I Ep. 138
episodes.description:
The most chilling cult stories aren’t always about strangers. Sometimes the cult is your last name.

Stella McCormick, author of Deliver Us from Mother: Faith, Fear, and the Family Cult That Broke Me, joins Ingrid to share what it was like growing up inside what she now recognizes as a single-family cult—an extreme fundamentalist Christian home shaped by isolation, fear, unquestioned authority, and punishment disguised as discipline.

But Stella didn’t always recognize her childhood as abuse.

Years later, after surviving a military sexual assault and beginning therapy during an overseas deployment, one unexpected question from her therapist forced Stella to reconsider everything she had been taught was normal. What followed was the painful recognition of childhood trauma, a lifetime spent in survival mode, and the realization that younger siblings were still living under the same control.

Stella and Ingrid explore the intersection of religious trauma, coercive control, spiritual abuse, and domestic violence—and how the same tactics can appear across each: isolation, gaslighting, love bombing, fear, and control.

They also discuss mental health stigma in fundamentalist Christian environments, panic attacks, medication, faith deconstruction, and the BITE Model developed by Steven Hassan, which finally gave Stella language for what she had experienced.

Because sometimes recognizing abuse means questioning the very things you were taught never to question.

In this episode: religious trauma, coercive control, family cults, spiritual abuse, high-control religion, the BITE Model, fundamentalist Christianity, childhood trauma, military sexual assault, domestic violence, faith deconstruction, and trauma recovery.

This podcast is intended for mature audiences. Some listeners may find the content distressing as episodes may include discussions of violence, human trafficking, and other forms of abuse, including emotional, psychological, sexual, financial, and physical. In many cases, names have been changed to protect those involved. Please note that the statements and opinions expressed by guests do not necessarily reflect my own.

If you are in the United States and need immediate support, contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline by calling 800-799-SAFE (7233) or texting START to 88788. If you're outside the United States, crisis resources are available at BeyondTheStatisticsPodcast.com/GetHelp.

If today's conversation meant something to you, please subscribe, leave a review, and share this episode. Every story shared helps another survivor know they are not alone.

Music: Tim Crowe
